summary: Gives the spine one entry point that owns every surface a summary drives -- the record counter, the three gauge numbers, the three gauge arcs and what EXPORT FILTERED CSV writes -- and has the wider-fleet cut call it, so its figures stop being the previous technology's and its export declines in words instead of emitting the spine's rows.
modification_note: The record counter, the gauge numbers, the gauge arcs and the CSV export were all derived from a summary computed in two places. The spine's apply() drove the counter and the gauges; the wider-fleet cartridge recomputed the same quantities and wrote only the gauge text. Everything it did not write kept the previous technology's answer on all twenty wider-fleet technologies -- the counter's four figures and its dataset, and the three gauge arcs, which are painted by updateChart and were byte-identical on toDataURL across a switch. EXPORT FILTERED CSV was worse: it mapped the spine's `filtered` array, which holds indices into the spine's own payload, so one flywheel on screen exported 3,563 solar rows and reported that count as fact. This release replaces the duplicated calculation with presentSummary(), which the spine's apply() and the cartridge's renderWider() both call, and which owns all four surfaces. A cut that is not the spine's own supplies an export provider; the wider fleet's declines, naming the ten of the CSV's fifty columns it could fill and what the other forty are. No spine behaviour changes: apply() passes no provider, so the product's own export path is the one it always was.

app.from: invariant(result.controlsAdded === 1, "wider fleet put more than one control in the technology row");
app.to:
invariant(result.controlsAdded === 1, "wider fleet put more than one control in the technology row");
  invariant(result.exportPolicy === "declines", "wider fleet started writing the spine 50-column CSV");

edits.label: the contract names the seam and the export policy
edits.to:
control_in_product_technology_row: "select",
  deep_linkable: true,
  /* Every figure this cut puts on a surface the spine owns goes through the
     one function the spine hands over at mount -- the counter, the three
     gauge numbers, the three gauge arcs, and what EXPORT FILTERED CSV does.
     Writing any of them here again is the defect this replaced. */
  drives_summary_seam: true,
  export_policy: "declines",
  reads_spine_payload: false,

edits.label: what this cut could honestly export, and the refusal
clearing hands the surfaces back
renderWider calls the seam instead of writing gauges
edits.to:
/* ONE CALL, EVERY SURFACE A SUMMARY DRIVES.

       This block used to write #v1/#v2/#v3 by hand, and only those. The three
       gauge ARCS are painted by the spine's updateChart against the canvases
       g1/g2/g3, which nothing here could reach, so the ring went on showing
       the previous technology's proportion with this technology's number
       printed inside it -- verified by comparing toDataURL across a switch,
       identical byte for byte. The record counter above the table was never
       written at all, and EXPORT FILTERED CSV went on believing it held the
       spine's rows.

       Handing the figures to the spine's seam instead makes those four
       surfaces one decision. The arcs are drawn against the spine's own
       register totals, exactly as they are for its own four tabs, so the ring
       and the number inside it are now the same measurement.

       `total` is this cut's own 1,104 rows, not the spine's 7,680: there is
       no flywheel in the spine's register, and "1 of 7,680 records" would
       have been a new wrong number. The export provider declines and says
       what it cannot fill; it is a function so that it is answered against
       the rows on screen at the moment of the click, not at render time. */
    presentSummary({
      count: shown.length,
      total: rows.length,
      capacity: Number(megawatts.toFixed(2)),
      largest,
      exportProvider: (request) => declineExport(request, active, shown),
    });

edits.label: the mount report states the export policy
edits.to:
controlsAdded: 1,
    optionsAdded: options.length,
    /* Stated to app.mjs so a change of mind about the CSV cannot be a
       silent one: it invariants this value at mount. */
    exportPolicy: "declines",

edits.label: the refusal gets its own line and the warning colour

set.mutation_scope: appends one label and one select to #tech; while one of that select's twenty technologies is chosen it paints .tablewrap tbody and calls the spine's presentSummary() seam, which drives #resultsMeta, the three gauge values and the three gauge arcs, and installs an export provider that declines the spine's 50-column CSV in words
set.presentation: one labelled select carrying twenty REPD technology types, each with its own project count; the spine's five tabs are unchanged; the record counter, gauges and gauge arcs follow the chosen technology, and EXPORT FILTERED CSV refuses for these rows and names the columns it cannot fill
